tagline: Over the mountain into the valley the Vanderbilts could not buy.
intro: From SR 61 at Gratton, Burkes Garden Road climbs over Garden Mountain and comes down into an oval bowl of farmland around 3,000 feet up, the second highest valley in Virginia, and the byway then loops around the valley on Medley Valley, West End, Banks Ridge and Gose Mill roads. On a map the bowl looks like a crater. It is an eroded dome, where soft limestone wore away inside a ring of harder sandstone ridges.
In the late 1800s agents for the Vanderbilts came asking to buy land for an estate. Nobody would sell, and the family built Biltmore near Asheville instead.

moments.title: Garden Mountain
moments.text: On the way in, the road crosses the Appalachian Trail, which keeps to the ridge of Garden Mountain with views down into the bowl.

moments.title: Burke's Garden
moments.text: A surveying party of 1748 came back a year later to find potatoes growing where James Burke had thrown out his peelings, and the joke name stuck.

moments.title: Central Lutheran Church
moments.text: The county's oldest church started as a Union Church for several denominations, and when it went Lutheran most of the congregation left to found Methodist and Presbyterian churches.
